description: Enzyme catalyzing the reversible phosphorolytic cleavage of purine and pyrimidine ribonucleosides, liberating the free nucleobase together with alpha-D-ribose 1-phosphate; accepts inosine, xanthosine, adenosine, cytidine and uridine as substrates and functions in nucleotide salvage metabolism.

Sequence-specific transcriptional regulator of the basic helix-loop-helix superfamily that recognizes defined promoter elements at RNA polymerase II regulatory regions and modulates gene expression as a component of a nuclear transcription-factor assembly.

Component of the fatty-acid biosynthetic machinery that eliminates water from (3R)-3-hydroxyacyl-carrier-protein intermediates and isomerizes the product, installing a cis double bond during lipid chain elongation; most active on medium-chain hydroxyacyl species.

Membrane-embedded ATP-driven zinc metalloprotease that processively degrades cytoplasmic and integral-membrane substrates; coordinates a catalytic zinc ion, hydrolyzes ATP, spans the bilayer through helical segments, and bears an N-terminal targeting signal.
Amino-acid biosynthetic enzyme relying on a catalytic proton-accepting residue that contributes to the diaminopimelate route toward lysine and to de novo methionine production.

Post-replicative mismatch-repair factor recognizing small insertion loops within MutS-type complexes, binding magnesium and hydrolyzing ATP, cooperating with MutL partners in the nucleus, and feeding into p53-dependent apoptotic signaling after genomic damage.
Isomerase of the histidine biosynthetic pathway that rearranges the phosphoribosyl-aminoimidazole-carboxamide (ProFAR) intermediate into its ketose isomer with high substrate affinity.
Cytoplasmic GTP-hydrolyzing translation factor with a translational-type G domain that escorts aminoacyl-tRNA to the ribosomal acceptor site in a GTP-dependent fashion during polypeptide elongation.
Plasma-membrane transport protein carrying an N-terminal RCK regulatory module together with helical membrane-spanning segments that govern ion conductance across the lipid bilayer.

Nucleotide-sugar biosynthetic enzyme condensing a UTP-activated donor with N-acetylglucosamine 1-phosphate to form UDP-N-acetylglucosamine, requiring magnesium and supporting cell-envelope and cell-shape maintenance.
